item.title: Dominant Role of Solid Matrix and Persistent Free Radicals in Cr(VI) Reduction by Biochar
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Zhe Ding, Jianjun Liang, Longmiao Yuan, Wentao Zhang, Beihang Zhang, Huiyang Mei 等8位作者
Biochar has emerged as a promising material for remediating toxic hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)), yet the distinct roles of its soluble components and solid matrix remain poorly understood. This study systematically investigated the mechanisms of Cr(VI) immobilization by rice husk biochar produced at different pyrolysis temperatures (200–600°C). The biochar pyrolyzed at 400°C (RH400) exhibits the highest Cr(VI) reduction efficiency, effectively converting Cr(VI) to less toxic Cr(III). Through comparative experiments with biochar leachate and the residual solid matrix, we demonstrate that the soluble leachate does not contribute to Cr(VI) reduction, but instead antagonizes total chromium immobilization by competing for sorption sites. item.title: Initial Conformation Governs Amyloid-β42 Dynamics and Association at a POPC Membrane-Water Interface
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Yersultan Arynbek, Khlood A.A.A. Abdeljawaad, Duc Huy Le, Kahramon Mamatkulov, Grigory Arzumanyan
The conformational heterogeneity of amyloid-β42 (Aβ42) may influence its early interactions with lipid membranes, yet the extent to which different initial structures determine subsequent membrane association remains unclear. Here, three nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) derived Aβ42 monomer structures (1IYT, 1Z0Q, and 6SZF) were examined at a 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-phosphocholine (POPC) membrane-water interface. Despite an identical environment, the monomers followed different trajectories during comparative 200-ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulations using the CHARMM36m force field. The predominantly α-helical 1IYT structure underwent substantial relaxation, with α-helical content decreasing from 78.57% to 44.77%. item.title: Synergistic Dual-Reinforcement of Carbon Fiber/Polycarbonate Thermoplastic Composites via Molecularly Designed Interfacial Modification and Interlaminar Nano-Bridging
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Chin-Hsing Chen, Yi-Ru Liu, Ming-Yuan Shen, Chien-Hung Liu
Carbon fiber-reinforced thermoplastic (CFRTP) composites present a recyclable alternative to traditional thermosets, yet fully realizing their structural potential remains constrained by the chemical incompatibility between commercial epoxy-based sizing on the surface of carbon fibers and high-viscosity thermoplastic matrices such as polycarbonate (PC). To overcome this bottleneck, this study introduces a multiscale synergistic dual-reinforcement strategy that couples molecularly designed interfacial modification with strategic interlaminar nano-bridging. item.title: Experimental Correlation of Electrical and Optical Noise in a DFB Laser: Implications for Quantum Key Distribution and Quantum Random Number Generation
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Imad ASAAD
We present an experimental and analytical study of the electrical-optical noise correlation in a distributed-feedback (DFB) laser diode operating at 1550 nm. Using dual-channel fast Fourier transform (FFT) measurements, we extract the power spectral densities of the injection current noise, the relative intensity noise (RIN) and their cross-spectrum. From these, the spectral coherence CI−P (f ) is computed, revealing a strong correlation at low frequencies ( 0.82). We quantify the impact of this correlation on two quantum communication technologies. For quantum key distribution (QKD), we evaluate the information leakage and show that with standard low-noise electronics it remains negligible.
